details: Bitcoin and Ethereum are experiencing significant institutional outflows from their respective Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs). US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $1.47 billion in outflows last week, marking the second consecutive week of redemptions and bringing the two-week total to $2.54 billion. This decline is largely attributed to the US Treasury market signaling that interest rates will remain elevated for longer than anticipated, creating a challenging environment for risk assets like cryptocurrencies. Geopolitical tensions, particularly involving the Middle East, and persistent inflation fears are further contributing to market volatility and a "risk-off" sentiment, pushing Bitcoin prices to struggle around key support levels in the mid-$70,000 range.
title: Bitcoin & Ethereum Face Pressure Amid ETF Outflows, Geopolitical Tensions

details: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has reportedly paused plans to allow crypto operators to tokenize equities without the consent of the issuing company. This delay, initially reported by Bloomberg, stems from concerns raised by traditional stock exchanges and other market participants regarding investor protection, ownership verification on decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms, and the enforcement of shareholder rights like dividends and voting. This regulatory setback highlights ongoing challenges in integrating digital assets with traditional financial markets.
title: SEC Pauses Tokenized Stock Plans Amid Regulatory Concerns

details: The cryptocurrency market is closely monitoring key U.S. macroeconomic indicators this week, including PCE inflation, initial jobless claims, and housing data. These figures will be crucial in determining the Federal Reserve's flexibility to adjust interest rates. Current market sentiment, supported by tools like the CME FedWatch, strongly suggests the Fed will maintain its current interest rates in June. Persistent inflation and geopolitical developments, particularly fluctuating oil prices, could further exacerbate inflationary pressures, impacting risk asset performance and potentially delaying any monetary easing.
title: US Macro Data and Fed Rate Speculations to Influence Crypto Markets
